issues.legal_issue: An agent’s power of attorney is irrevocable after the principal’s death under Section 202 of the Contract Act only when the agent has an interest in the subject matter of the agency, and that interest must be secured by the agency rather than arise merely from an agreement to sell or the power of attorney’s description as irrevocable.

An unregistered agreement to sell and power of attorney, whether read separately or together, do not transfer title or create an enforceable interest in immovable property where registration is required.

A registered sale deed executed by a power-of-attorney holder after the principal’s death does not convey valid title when the agency had terminated and the power of attorney was not coupled with an interest.

A court may decide title in a suit for injunction without a separate prayer for declaration when title is directly and substantially in issue, the pleadings and issues raise it, and determining title is necessary to decide possession and the injunction.
